title: 100 GRPO Steps to Make a 350M Model Respect Your Schema
hook: Small models are cheap but sloppy about output format. Three simple programmatic rewards and about 500 samples nearly doubled a 350M model's JSON pass rate.
key_points: Target: structured output compliance — does the model actually return the JSON or YAML shape you asked for?
Model is LiquidAI's LFM2.5-350M, trained with GRPO in TRL for 100 steps on roughly 500 samples.
Three reward functions: JSON format validity, field count accuracy, and schema validation — all programmatic, no reward model.
Overall IFStruct score went 22.6% to 29.7% (+7.1 points); JSON format pass rate 18.0% to 31.9% (+13.9 points).
Bare list structure improved 16.6% to 29.7%, while YAML barely moved (27.2% to 27.5%).
content_html: Ask a small model for JSON matching a schema and you'll often get nearly JSON. Monigatti and collaborators from Hugging Face and Liquid AI walk through fixing that with reinforcement learning on Liquid AI's LFM2.5-350M — a run small enough to reproduce, using GRPO in the TRL library over roughly 500 samples and 100 steps.
extra_html:
How it works

The appeal here is that the reward needs no reward model. Structured output is programmatically checkable, so the post details three reward functions: is the output valid JSON, does it have the right number of fields, and does it validate against the requested schema. GRPO then optimizes against that composite signal.

Why it matters

The reported gains on the IFStruct benchmark are concentrated exactly where the rewards pointed: overall score from 22.6% to 29.7% (+7.1 points), JSON format pass rate from 18.0% to 31.9% (+13.9 points), and bare-list structure from 16.6% to 29.7% (+13.1 points). YAML, which the rewards didn't target, barely budged at 27.2% to 27.5%. That asymmetry is the real lesson: verifiable rewards work, and they improve precisely what you chose to verify.

flashcards.prompt: Why is structured-output compliance a good fit for GRPO rather than a learned reward model?
flashcards.back_html: The reward is programmatically checkable — you can parse the JSON, count fields, and validate against the schema — so you get exact, cheap signals with no reward model to train.

flashcards.prompt: Which format saw almost no improvement in this run?
flashcards.explanation_html: JSON format pass rate jumped +13.9 points and bare lists +13.1, but YAML moved only 0.3 points — the rewards were JSON-shaped, and that's what improved.

flashcards.prompt: How much training did this take?
flashcards.back_html: About 500 samples over 100 GRPO steps on a 350M-parameter model — small enough to be a realistic afternoon experiment.
